question: What are the right discipline, grade and disciplines list for McLoughlin East Ridge, a summer trail plus class 2 scree/scramble walk-up that is a snow climb in winter/spring?
answer: In summer it is a trail (about 9.6 mi round trip, 3,900 ft gain) ending in short rock scrambles with hand use, mostly class 2 with some class 3 per a climber's log; helmets advised. Winter from Hwy 140 is cross-country snow with ice axe, crampons or snowshoes, cornices and avalanche exposure on the upper ridge. There is no roped or technical element, so by owner rule it is mountaineering (non-technical walk-up). The grade 'Easy Snow' misdescribes the summer climb.
recommendation: Keep discipline mountaineering; set disciplines to ["mountaineering"] only (drop alpine: nothing roped or technical); set grade to 'Class 2' (summer scramble; snow in season). Put the winter/spring snow, axe and avalanche notes in the prose and season (Jul-Oct dry; Nov-Jun snow).
